title: Vacuum breaker leaking: top, vent, or hose connection?
description: Locate a leaking vacuum breaker and distinguish PVB startup spillage, continuous bonnet discharge, freeze cracks, and hose-bib leakage before choosing parts.
answer: Vacuum breakers intentionally admit air, so the vent cannot be sealed. A short event during pressure change is not the same evidence as continuous flow or a cracked bonnet.
urgency: Do not cap the vent. Isolate only through a known safe procedure, especially when freezing or flooding is possible.
diagramAlt: Pressure vacuum breaker diagram marking bonnet, air inlet, and body leak points
identifiers: Start-up or shutdown only: record how long the release lasts.
Continuous from the bonnet: debris, sealing, pressure, or damage may need service.
From a visible crack: freeze damage is more likely than a replaceable seal alone.

choices.label: Briefly when irrigation starts or stops
choices.detail: Observe duration, frequency, and whether the poppet reseats.

choices.label: Continuously from the top or vent
choices.detail: Do not block it; arrange inspection before water damage or freezing.

choices.label: From a cracked bonnet or body
choices.detail: Compare replacement scope and any required retest.

choices.label: At an outdoor faucet attachment
choices.detail: Confirm it is a hose-bib device, not a testable PVB.

steps.title: Identify PVB, AVB, or hose-bib
steps.body: The repair path depends on the actual device family.

steps.title: Observe one complete cycle
steps.body: Record before start, during flow, shutdown, and several minutes after.

steps.title: Check local consequences
steps.body: A testable irrigation assembly may require a test after repair or replacement.

safeChecks: Look for freeze cracks and loose external fittings.
Record the make, model, pipe size, and installation height.
stopConditions: Unknown shutoff or a commercial system
notThisDevice: An RPZ relief valve is below a larger inline body.
A pressure regulator does not use an atmospheric air inlet.
A sewer valve does not discharge clean supply water.
evidenceNote: The page owns the observable leak decision. It does not duplicate model-specific repair instructions or invent a local testing rule.

fieldSections.title: Where and when is the vacuum breaker leaking?
fieldSections.introduction: Record a full start/run/stop cycle from a safe distance. The 800M4 manual describes startup spillage while its air inlet is still open; persistent flow needs a different assessment.

rows.observation: PVB top / air inlet at startup
rows.meaning: A brief event while pressure builds can differ from a leak that continues during steady operation.
rows.nextStep: Record duration and whether the release stops. Follow the exact startup instructions; do not improvise valve operation.

rows.meaning: Timing alone cannot distinguish debris, seals, pressure conditions, or damage.
rows.nextStep: Keep the vent open and request a model-specific inspection.

rows.observation: Bonnet, body, or fitting with a visible crack
rows.meaning: A damaged pressure boundary changes repair scope; a seal kit may not solve it.
rows.nextStep: Avoid pressurized disassembly; compare qualified replacement and retest scope.

rows.observation: Hose-end vent after shutting off the faucet
rows.meaning: First establish that this is a hose-bib vacuum breaker, not a testable PVB.
rows.nextStep: Compare the attachment type and manufacturer instructions.
